cohort: The study included 5011 patients who delivered at a large medical center in South Carolina between 2019 and 2020.
finding: Non-Hispanic Black mothers were more likely to have cesarean deliveries compared to non-Hispanic White mothers, a disparity that was explained by census tract differences in the Social Vulnerability Index.
mod_finding: Non-Hispanic Black mothers exhibited a higher prevalence of cesarean deliveries, an association that became non-significant after controlling for census tract-level Social Vulnerability Index.
